analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It adds a documented `darkbloom status` runtime-integrity line (head lines 986-991). The line appears when the coordinator's latest `runtime_status` marked this provider's runtime hashes outdated. It shows the mismatch count, says the provider is excluded from routing, and points to `darkbloom update`. The line clears itself once the record is over 15 minutes old. I examined both base units (lines 808-1288 and 1289-1682) and the patch. No code, authentication, encryption, authorization or routing behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so no control is weakened and no new attack surface is introduced.

Relevant threat IDs are TB-002, TB-009, T-034, T-036 and T-053. The documentation says the coordinator keeps sending `verified:false` while a mismatch lasts. It also says the local display expires after 15 minutes. That reads as a local status display, not a trust or authorization decision, and the coordinator remains authoritative. Residual questions for deeper review: whether the provider's `runtime_status` handler exists in the code (not supplied), and whether the expiry only hides the warning without any serving or authorization effect. A coordinator, or anyone able to spoof coordinator messages, could trigger the line. That is no worse than the existing trusted-coordinator model, because the line only says 'run darkbloom update', and the update path verifies hashes (SelfUpdater, documented at base lines 1405-1406). The documented implementation is not in this batch, so no code-level conclusion is possible.
